reason: Full Auto was refusing every orchestration launch, including ones the person started, and the first diagnosis wrongly blamed a halt. The rule separating automatic from person-started launches, and the check on halt flags, belong in one class-level skill for launch gating.
Stop-all was used as a brake without asking, and it silently turned Full Auto off, so the person's paused work stayed paused until they re-enabled it.

The body already forbids stop-all as a brake and says it switches Full Auto off, but the description only matches a refused start. The agent stopped all agents without loading this skill, so the description must also trigger on stops and Full Auto toggles.

The agent scheduled a background self-stop of its own runner to pick up new code. The person objected at once, so a stop or restart is a person's decision even when it is only the agent's own session.
Its Full Auto gate and stop-all rules move to references/full-auto-stops-and-starts.md, linked from the umbrella's Full Auto section.
